findings.explanation: The on-node cmdlet is Get-AzureStackHCI. It returns ClusterStatus (Clustered/OutOfPolicy), RegistrationStatus, RegistrationDate, AzureResourceName, AzureResourceUri, ConnectionStatus, LastConnected, NextSync, IMDSAttestation and DiagnosticLevel. It does not return ClusterName, Status, BillingStatus or LastBillingTimestamp, and no Get-AzureStackHciCluster cmdlet exists on nodes. As written, the poller contract cannot be implemented, and the fields the alert keys on would be empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Document Get-AzureStackHCI and its real properties (ClusterStatus, RegistrationStatus, ConnectionStatus, LastConnected, NextSync). Take ClusterName from (Get-Cluster).Name and add it in the poller. Use LastConnected and ClusterStatus=OutOfPolicy for the billing/sync-age tier.

findings.explanation: Az.StackHCI is the Azure PowerShell module used from a management host (Register-AzStackHCI and so on). The node-side status cmdlet Get-AzureStackHCI ships with the OS AzureStackHCI module. The step therefore points operators at the wrong module and a nonexistent cmdlet. The implementation field repeats the Az.StackHCI instruction.
findings.quote: imports `Az.StackHCI` on that side if needed, then calls `Get-AzureStackHciCluster` for billing and registration
findings.suggested_fix: Run Invoke-Command -ComputerName <node> { Get-AzureStackHCI } without importing Az.StackHCI on the node, and reserve Az.StackHCI for optional Azure-side queries.

findings.explanation: This is authoring residue left in published guidance. It also introduces unrelated content (Exchange on HCI, AVD GPU hosts) that dilutes the runbook.
findings.quote: Filler to guarantee length: capacity reviews should reference this saved search’s CSV export.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the 'Filler to guarantee length' paragraph and keep only the actionable tuning note about deriving long_run_sec thresholds from observed rebuild durations.

findings.explanation: This is generator-cleanup commentary, not a scope exclusion. Calling the custom poller sourcetypes 'real' is also misleading, because they are names the customer defines.
findings.quote: The templated sourcetype `azurestackhci:health` is fictional; real sourcetypes are the `windows:azurestackhci:*` and optional `azure:resource:graph` families
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the sentence and keep only actual out-of-scope statements.

findings.explanation: The SPL hard-codes freeze_active=1 to severity 'ok' before any other branch is evaluated. A down node or unhealthy pool during a freeze is therefore silently classed ok and cannot be routed to a low-urgency channel as the text describes.
findings.quote: When `freeze_active=1` from the lookup, route to a low-urgency channel or suppress entirely, depending on your change practice.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual behaviour (a freeze forces ok), or state that a separate demotion step is needed if freeze rows must still surface.

findings.explanation: MSFT_StorageJob JobState follows the CIM ConcreteJob enumeration (New, Starting, Running, Suspended, ShuttingDown, Completed, Terminated, Killed, Exception, ...). 'Failed' does not appear to be a value, so failure detection keyed on it would miss real failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the enumeration against the Microsoft Storage Management API MSFT_StorageJob reference and list the actual terminal-failure states.

findings.explanation: The UC does not show that either 3757 or 3110 ships a Resource Graph input emitting these sourcetypes, and the text itself admits the names are guessed.
findings.quote: Kusto/Resource Graph via Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Azure (3757) into `azure:resource:graph` or the closely related `mscs:azure:resource:graph` (vendor packaging determines the second name)
findings.suggested_fix: Check the input types and sourcetypes in the 3757 and 3110 documentation. If no Resource Graph input exists, describe a custom Resource Graph REST poller instead.

findings.explanation: Asterisk is a VoIP PBX and has nothing to do with Azure Stack HCI, so this tag puts the UC on the wrong equipment page.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'asterisk'; keep azure and hyperv, plus windows if the registry has it.

findings.explanation: The HEC link is truncated to a directory. The 'Use PowerShell to manage Azure Stack HCI' link points to the product hub root rather than a PowerShell page. Neither lands on the cited content.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/Data/UsetheHTTPEventCollector and the Microsoft Learn page documenting Get-AzureStackHCI / cluster registration.

findings.explanation: The UC never mentions that Microsoft renamed Azure Stack HCI to Azure Local, which matters to operators searching current documentation and cmdlet references.
findings.quote: Alerts on Cluster Health anomalies for UC-19.2.21
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Azure Local (formerly Azure Stack HCI)' to the description and implementation text.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified even though its primary cluster stream names a nonexistent cmdlet and nonexistent properties. Its own hardware note says the field contract was 'tested conceptually'.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or community until the poller has been run against a real cluster.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: cluster_status, billing_status and last_billing_ts come from Status, BillingStatus and LastBillingTimestamp, which Get-AzureStackHCI does not emit (it emits ClusterStatus and LastConnected). The cls="error" critical branch, the billing OutOfPolicy high branch and the bill_age low branch can never fire.

In the 25-hour storage-job subsearch, run_dur is now()-_time for any event that was in state running. It never checks the job's latest state or groups by job. A job that finished hours ago still yields long_run_sec up to about 25 hours, so a cluster that ran any background S2D job in the last day escalates to high after 12 hours and critical after 24 hours. The main-window runsec has the same event-age-not-duration flaw.

On-prem ConnectionStatus values (for example Connected, RepairRegistrationRequired) and the Azure resource connectionStatus values (for example Connected, Disconnected, NotYetRegistered, NotConnectedRecently) use different vocabularies. In addition, uconn is "" rather than null when onprem_conn is empty, so mismatch can fire on non-issues.
The eval function is called as toString(...). The Search Reference documents tostring(); confirm that the mixed-case call is accepted, or normalise it.
sort 0 ClusterName, severity_bucket sorts severity labels lexically (critical, high, low, medium, ok), not by urgency.

summary: The node, pool and storage-job collection design is sensible, but the cluster/billing stream is built on a cmdlet and properties that do not exist. The real cmdlet is Get-AzureStackHCI, which has no ClusterName, Status, BillingStatus or LastBillingTimestamp, so the status and billing tiers can never fire. The text also carries authoring residue ('Filler to guarantee length', 'templated sourcetype ... is fictional') and an unrelated Asterisk equipment tag.
